card.title: Authority Changes Hands
card.instruction: Project control while guarding one detail that could transfer authority elsewhere. Let each return of that detail shift whom you defer to or overrule.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm chairing the club meeting until we locate the signed election result.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then may I respectfully propose we check both sides?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The back says the winner declined.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. My first decision is to store important documents face up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll chair the club meeting unless that signed result names someone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. May I ask you to check the date, Chair?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're right. My term starts next month.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll take questions. Yours first, if you raise your hand.

mechanism: A projects chairing authority but yields and regains it as the signed result and its date are examined.
confusable: Unlike defending power at any cost, A must actually defer when the guarded detail grants B authority.
comparison: S218-a changes who answers questions through an election date; S218-b changes the rehearsal time through key access.

bindingFindings.assessment: Unsafe to certify unchanged rebinding: although the authorization action and chairs-reverse opening identify a transferable authority detail, the comfortable-overlooking response and preservation closing keep A resisting inspection after the signature challenge. They do not demonstrate the instruction's required shifts of deference or command as the detail returns. Both current seeds enact a handover and recovery; both original seedBindingHashes now require integration rebinding, but that would not repair the transfer's behavioral gap. Leave transfer text, fingerprint, hashes and compiled-pair-draft status untouched pending separate review. No bespoke pairs or supporting seeds were supplied.

Not fully compatible with the exact instruction and supplied seeds: the action hides authorization, the opening acknowledges possible reversal, but the response and challenge/closing seek to overlook the detail and preserve control. Both seeds actually let the decisive detail produce deference and then restored authority. The transfer therefore omits the required recurring shift and favors concealment instead. Both seedIds resolve, but neither stored seedBindingHash matches its supplied candidateHash. Fingerprint and compiled-pair-draft status remain unchanged. No bespokePairs or supportingSeeds supply a compensating shift.

provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
